claim: Mice lacking IL10 have enhanced thermogenesis.
source: Mice lacking IL10 have enhanced thermogenesis, but the roles of specific cell types in the metabolic response to IL10 remain to be defined.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a known finding from prior work.

claim: Selective loss of IL10 receptor α in adipocytes recapitulates the beneficial effects of global IL10 deletion.
source: We demonstrate here that selective loss of IL10 receptor α in adipocytes recapitulates the beneficial effects of global IL10 deletion, and that local crosstalk between IL10-producing immune cells and adipocytes is a determinant of thermogenesis and systemic energy balance.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: Local crosstalk between IL10-producing immune cells and adipocytes is a determinant of thermogenesis and systemic energy balance.
source: We demonstrate here that selective loss of IL10 receptor α in adipocytes recapitulates the beneficial effects of global IL10 deletion, and that local crosstalk between IL10-producing immune cells and adipocytes is a determinant of thermogenesis and systemic energy balance.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data.

claim: Single Nuclei Adipocyte RNA-sequencing (SNAP-seq) of subcutaneous adipose tissue defined a metabolically-active mature adipocyte subtype characterized by robust expression of genes involved in thermogenesis.
source: Single Nuclei Adipocyte RNA-sequencing (SNAP-seq) of subcutaneous adipose tissue defined a metabolically-active mature adipocyte subtype characterized by robust expression of genes involved in thermogenesis whose transcriptome was selectively responsive to IL10Rα deletion.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by SNAP-seq data in the results.

claim: The transcriptome of the metabolically-active mature adipocyte subtype was selectively responsive to IL10Rα deletion.
source: Single Nuclei Adipocyte RNA-sequencing (SNAP-seq) of subcutaneous adipose tissue defined a metabolically-active mature adipocyte subtype characterized by robust expression of genes involved in thermogenesis whose transcriptome was selectively responsive to IL10Rα deletion.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by SNAP-seq data comparing control and knockout mice.

claim: Single-cell transcriptomic analysis of adipose stromal populations identified lymphocytes as a key source of IL10 production in response to thermogenic stimuli.
source: Furthermore, single-cell transcriptomic analysis of adipose stromal populations identified lymphocytes as a key source of IL10 production in response to thermogenic stimuli.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by scRNA-seq data of stromal vascular fraction.

claim: Adaptive immune cell-adipocyte communication is implicated in the maintenance of adipose subtype identity and function.
source: These findings implicate adaptive immune cell-adipocyte communication in the maintenance of adipose subtype identity and function.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the abstract based on the experimental findings.

claim: Adipose tissue plays an important role in the maintenance of energy balance in mammals.
source: Adipose tissue plays an important role in the maintenance of energy balance in mammals.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: A chronic imbalance between energy intake and expenditure increases adiposity and leads to obesity and predisposes to the development of metabolic disease.
source: A chronic imbalance between energy intake and expenditure increases adiposity and leads to obesity and predisposes to the development of metabolic disease (Rosen and Spiegelman, 2014; Wajchenberg, 2000).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with supporting citations.

claim: White adipose tissue (WAT) is essential for triglyceride (TG) storage.
source: White adipose tissue (WAT) is essential for triglyceride (TG) storage, whereas thermogenic brown adipose tissue (BAT) dissipates energy as heat through mitochondrial uncoupling mechanisms including uncoupling protein 1 (UCP1) (Cannon and Nedergaard, 2004; Chechi et al., 2013; Saely et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with supporting citations.

claim: Thermogenic brown adipose tissue (BAT) dissipates energy as heat through mitochondrial uncoupling mechanisms including uncoupling protein 1 (UCP1).
source: White adipose tissue (WAT) is essential for triglyceride (TG) storage, whereas thermogenic brown adipose tissue (BAT) dissipates energy as heat through mitochondrial uncoupling mechanisms including uncoupling protein 1 (UCP1) (Cannon and Nedergaard, 2004; Chechi et al., 2013; Saely et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with supporting citations.

claim: A subpopulation of mature adipocytes in certain WAT depots, known as beige adipocytes, acquires thermogenic capacity in response to cold or hormonal stimuli.
source: A subpopulation of mature adipocytes in certain WAT depots, known as beige adipocytes, also acquires thermogenic capacity in response to cold or hormonal stimuli.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: Increasing the activity of thermogenic adipocytes in animal models counteracts the development of obesity and diabetes.
source: Increasing the activity of thermogenic adipocytes in animal models counteracts the development of obesity and diabetes (Cohen et al., 2014; Harms and Seale, 2013; Song et al., 2016; Villanueva et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with supporting citations.

claim: White adipocytes mobilize stored lipids through hydrolysis of triglycerides and release of free fatty acid in times of metabolic need.
source: In times of metabolic need, white adipocytes mobilize stored lipids through hydrolysis of triglycerides and release of free fatty acid (Zechner et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a supporting citation.

claim: Activation of β-adrenergic receptors (β-ARs) by catecholamines released by the sympathetic nervous system (SNS) is a major physiological inducer of lipolysis and adipose thermogenesis.
source: Activation of β-adrenergic receptors (β-ARs) by catecholamines released by the sympathetic nervous system (SNS) is a major physiological inducer of lipolysis and adipose thermogenesis (Bartness et al., 2014; Harms and Seale, 2013; Vitali et al., 2012; Wang et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with supporting citations.

claim: Cold sensation triggers β-AR activation in adipose tissue, resulting in cAMP production and the activation of protein kinase A (PKA) and p38 kinase.
source: Cold sensation triggers β-AR activation in adipose tissue, resulting in cAMP production and the activation of protein kinase A (PKA) and p38 kinase.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: PKA and p38 kinase initiate phosphorylation cascades that impinge on C/EBP, ATF, and CREB transcription factors that regulate the expression of genes involved in mitochondrial biogenesis and thermogenesis.
source: These kinases initiate phosphorylation cascades that impinge on C/EBP, ATF, and CREB transcription factors that regulate the expression of gene involved in mitochondrial biogenesis (such as Ppargc1) and thermogenesis (such as Ucp1) (Harms and Seale, 2013).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a supporting citation.

claim: Adrenergic stimuli induce lipolysis in adipocytes through PKA-dependent phosphorylation of lipases including hormone-sensitive lipase (HSL) and adipose triglyceride lipase (ATGL).
source: Adrenergic stimuli induce lipolysis in adipocytes through PKA-dependent phosphorylation of lipases including hormone-sensitive lipase (HSL) and adipose triglyceride lipase (ATGL) (Duncan et al., 2007; Jaworski et al., 2007; Zechner et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with supporting citations.

claim: Free fatty acid (FA) released from adipocytes can be used by peripheral tissues for mitochondrial respiration.
source: Free fatty acid (FA) released from adipocytes can be used by peripheral tissues for mitochondrial respiration.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: Genetic deletion of β-ARs or adipocyte-specific loss of ATGL causes a drastic reduction in energy expenditure that predisposes mice to obesity.
source: The importance of β-AR-dependent lipid mobilization and thermogenesis is underscored by the observations that genetic deletion of β-ARs or adipocyte-specific loss of ATGL causes a drastic reduction in energy expenditure that predisposes mice to obesity (Bachman et al., 2002; Schreiber et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with supporting citations.

claim: Clearance of catecholamine is critical in terminating β-adrenergic signals.
source: Clearance of catecholamine is critical in terminating β-adrenergic signals, and local catabolism of catecholamine is an established mechanism for negative regulation of adrenergic signaling in adipose tissue (Camell et al., 2017; Pirzgalska et al., 2017; Song et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with supporting citations.

claim: Local catabolism of catecholamine is an established mechanism for negative regulation of adrenergic signaling in adipose tissue.
source: Clearance of catecholamine is critical in terminating β-adrenergic signals, and local catabolism of catecholamine is an established mechanism for negative regulation of adrenergic signaling in adipose tissue (Camell et al., 2017; Pirzgalska et al., 2017; Song et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with supporting citations.

claim: Prior studies revealed an unexpected role for IL10 signaling in the inhibition of β-adrenergic signaling and adipose thermogenesis.
source: However, our prior studies revealed an unexpected role for IL10 signaling in the inhibition of β-adrenergic signaling and adipose thermogenesis (Rajbhandari et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from prior work with a citation.

claim: Mice globally-deficient in IL10 expression have enhanced energy expenditure and are protected from diet-induced obesity.
source: Mice globally-deficient in IL10 expression have enhanced energy expenditure and are protected from diet-induced obesity.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from prior work in the introduction.

claim: Chromatin accessibility at thermogenic genes in subcutaneous adipose tissue was linked to IL10 signaling.
source: We showed that chromatin accessibility at thermogenic genes in subcutaneous adipose tissue was linked to IL10 signaling; however, whether adipocytes themselves are the primary target for the metabolic effects of IL10 in vivo remains to be established.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from prior work with a citation.

claim: Adipocyte-specific deletion of IL10Rα increases adipose adrenergic signaling.
source: Here, we show that adipocyte-specific deletion of IL10Rα increases adipose adrenergic signaling, recapitulating the effects of whole-body IL10 deletion.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the introduction and supported by experimental data.

claim: Single nuclei transcriptomics of mature subcutaneous adipocytes identified a thermogenic adipocyte subtype that was enriched in IL10Rα-deficient mice.
source: Single nuclei transcriptomics of mature subcutaneous adipocytes identified a thermogenic adipocyte subtype that was enriched in IL10Rα-deficient mice.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the introduction and supported by SNAP-seq data.

claim: Single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-Seq) of adipose stromal populations revealed an increase in IL10-producing adaptive immune cells under adrenergic stimulation.
source: Additionally, single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-Seq) of adipose stromal populations revealed an increase in IL10-producing adaptive immune cells under adrenergic stimulation.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the introduction and supported by scRNA-seq data.

claim: There was no difference in body weight or food intake between 10 week-old chow-fed AdIL10Rα KO mice and floxed littermate controls.
source: There was no difference in body weight or food intake between 10 week-old chow-fed AdIL10Rα KO mice and floxed littermate controls (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and B.

claim: Metabolic cage analysis revealed increased oxygen consumption and energy expenditure in AdIL10Rα KO mice, without changes in locomotion and body mass.
source: However, metabolic cage analysis revealed increased oxygen consumption and energy expenditure in AdIL10Rα KO mice, without changes in locomotion and body mass (Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: After 8–9 weeks of HFD feeding, both male and female AdIL10Rα KO mice were protected against weight gain compared to floxed littermate controls.
source: After 8–9 weeks of HFD feeding, both male and female AdIL10Rα KO mice were protected against weight gain compared to floxed littermate controls (Figure 1C,D and Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).

claim: MRI analysis of body composition showed that the difference in body weight was entirely due to a change in fat mass.
source: MRI analysis of body composition showed that the difference in body weight was entirely due to a change in fat mass (Figure 1E).

claim: The inguinal WAT (iWAT) of AdIL10Rα KO mice was visibly redder than that of controls, suggesting increased tissue 'browning'.
source: Consistent with these findings, the inguinal WAT (iWAT) of AdIL10Rα KO mice was visibly redder than that of controls, suggesting increased tissue 'browning' (Figure 1F).

claim: Analysis of iWAT gene expression by real-time PCR showed increased expression of Ucp1, Elovl3, Ppargc1 and other thermogenic genes in AdIL10Rα KO mice exposed to cold stress.
source: Analysis of iWAT gene expression by real-time PCR showed increased expression of Ucp1, Elovl3, Ppargc1 and other thermogenic genes, but no change in general adipose markers such as Fabp4 and Pparg in AdIL10Rα KO mice (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: There was no change in general adipose markers such as Fabp4 and Pparg in AdIL10Rα KO mice exposed to cold stress.
source: Analysis of iWAT gene expression by real-time PCR showed increased expression of Ucp1, Elovl3, Ppargc1 and other thermogenic genes, but no change in general adipose markers such as Fabp4 and Pparg in AdIL10Rα KO mice (Figure 2A).

claim: RNA-seq on iWAT identified 214 genes that were enriched more than 1.5-fold in AdIL10Rα KO mice compared to control mice.
source: To gain insight into the global adipose gene expression changes in AdIL10Rα KO mice, we performed RNA-seq on iWAT. We identified 214 genes that were enriched more than 1.5-fold in AdIL10Rα KO mice compared to control mice (presented as a heatmap as a function of percentile expression in Figure 2C).
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The data revealed a selective increase in the thermogenic gene program in AdIL10Rα KO mice compared to controls.
source: The data revealed a selective increase in the thermogenic gene program in AdIL10Rα KO mice compared to controls.

claim: The gene expression differences between AdIL10Rα KO mice and controls were highly consistent with those observed in global IL10-deficient mice compared to WT controls.
source: The gene expression differences between AdIL10Rα KO mice and controls were highly consistent with those observed in global IL10-deficient mice compared to WT controls (Rajbhandari et al., 2018), strongly suggesting that the effects of IL10 on adipose tissue gene expression are mediated predominantly through direct action of IL10 on adipose IL10Rα.
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results with a citation to prior work.

claim: The effects of IL10 on adipose tissue gene expression are mediated predominantly through direct action of IL10 on adipose IL10Rα.
source: The gene expression differences between AdIL10Rα KO mice and controls were highly consistent with those observed in global IL10-deficient mice compared to WT controls (Rajbhandari et al., 2018), strongly suggesting that the effects of IL10 on adipose tissue gene expression are mediated predominantly through direct action of IL10 on adipose IL10Rα.

claim: Type nine adipocytes are confirmed as a bona-fide 'thermogenic adipocyte' cluster.

claim: Treatment of mice with CL increased the abundance of Type 9 cells to 23.5%.
